hints.title: Manager Subordinate Reporting Hierarchy
hints.text: Each employee has an optional reports_to field referencing their manager employee_id.

hints.title: Self-Joining on Manager Key
hints.text: join the employees table with itself where the manager employee_id equals the subordinate reports_to.

hints.title: Counting Reports and Rounding Average Age
hints.text: group by manager employee_id and name, aggregate with count for reports and round(avg(age)) for average age, and order by employee_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT m.employee_id, m.name,
       COUNT(e.employee_id) AS reports_count,
       ROUND(AVG(e.age)) AS average_age
FROM Employees m
JOIN Employees e ON m.employee_id = e.reports_to
GROUP BY m.employee_id, m.name
ORDER BY m.employee_id;
```

complexity.notes: Self-join on reports_to aggregates direct reports count and average age per manager.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Selecting all employees without joining only to reports_to produces individual subordinate profiles instead of manager summaries.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Joining manager and subordinate on indexed reports_to runs in linear O(N) time with bounded grouping state.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle self-joins for hierarchical reporting structures and rounding average age.
